env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

# Regression: importing a package whose generic function declares a local
# type ("entry·1" in export data) used to crash the compiler while the
# logos fact overlay eagerly resolved every name in the imported scope:
# "internal compiler error: unexpected object with N implicit type
# parameter(s)". Reported via bufbuild/protocompile internal/toposort.

cd w
go build ./...
go run ./main
stderr '^merged: 2$'

-- w/go.mod --
module example.com/icelocal

go 1.27

-- w/lib/lib.go --
package lib

import "cmp"

// Heap is a generic container whose type arguments let a caller's local
// types appear in this package's exported object table.
type Heap[K cmp.Ordered, V any] struct {
	n int
}

func NewHeap[K cmp.Ordered, V any](cap int) *Heap[K, V] {
	return &Heap[K, V]{n: cap}
}

func (h *Heap[K, V]) Len() int { return h.n }

// MergeKeySeq declares a local type inside a generic function. The
// compiler mangles it to "entry·N" with the function's four type
// parameters recorded as implicit type parameters in the object
// dictionary — a dictionary the import format forbids readers to load.
func MergeKeySeq[S ~[]E, E any, K cmp.Ordered, V any](
	slices []S,
	key func(slice int, elem E) K,
	mapper func(slice int, elem E) V,
) []V {
	type entry struct {
		index int
		slice S
	}
	heap := NewHeap[K, entry](len(slices))
	var out []V
	for i, slice := range slices {
		heap.Insert(key(i, slice[0]), entry{i, slice})
		out = append(out, mapper(i, slice[0]))
	}
	return out
}

func (h *Heap[K, V]) Insert(k K, v V) { h.n++ }

-- w/main/main.go --
package main

import "example.com/icelocal/lib"

func main() {
	got := lib.MergeKeySeq(
		[][]int{{1, 2}, {3}},
		func(_, e int) int { return e },
		func(_, e int) int { return e * 10 },
	)
	println("merged:", len(got))
}
